specification.title: A transaction writes a marker and fails with an application error
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Raise an application error inside the transaction, so that the framework rolls it back.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: A transaction that the API reports as rolled back is not committed: pg_xact_status() reports it aborted, and an independent connection does not see its marker.

execution.description: The same DataSource and the same DSL inserts. The application calls Connection.setAutoCommit(false) and Connection.commit or Connection.rollback. DSLContext.transaction is not called. A nested scope is Connection.setSavepoint, Connection.rollback(Savepoint), and Connection.releaseSavepoint on that connection. TX-05 calls Connection.setTransactionIsolation(TRANSACTION_SERIALIZABLE) before setAutoCommit(false). The connection stays open until after the after-end checkpoint, then closes. No pool. TX-03 is not run in this mode. This is the manual's JDBC-owned transaction, not a mitigation.

configuration.jooq: SQL execution only; DSLContext.transaction is not called
configuration.sql: DSL table and field names, no generated catalog

execution.form: Top-level transaction, then an insert into item through the DSL. Native mode is DSLContext.transaction. JDBC mode is Connection.setAutoCommit(false) and Connection.commit, with the same DSL insert.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The framework rolls the transaction back, and PostgreSQL confirms the ROLLBACK, so the client knows that nothing committed.

api_outcome.basis: the body threw and Connection.rollback() returned
api_outcome.contract: jOOQ 3.21 manual, Transaction management: jOOQ can run on a JDBC connection whose transaction the application already owns, by calling Connection.commit and Connection.rollback rather than DSLContext.transaction. This mode does not call DSLContext.transaction. A returning Connection.commit() is reported committed. The application's exception is reported rolled back only when Connection.rollback() returns. A thrown Connection.rollback() or Connection.commit() is reported failed: it asserts neither outcome. Connection.commit() is void and does not return a command tag. A nested scope is Connection.setSavepoint on the same connection.
